annotation.venue: Report of the State Comptroller of Israel – Cyber and Information Systems
named_instruments_referenced: Council of Europe Framework Convention on AI
annotation.summary_en: Israel State Comptroller audit of national AI preparedness (2018–2024). It finds no approved long-term national AI strategy, no integrating government body, slow Telem program budget execution, declining international rankings, and unapproved regulation and ethics policy principles. It recommends finalizing the national program and advancing regulation.
key_provisions_or_claims: Israel lacks a government-approved comprehensive national AI program six years after the 2018 decision.
No integrating government body is responsible for leading and supervising the national AI program.
Telem program first phase realized only ~40% of budget; the two phases total about one-fifth of the recommended budget.
AI regulation and ethics policy principles from the Innovation and Justice Ministries remain unapproved, while Israel lags the EU.
Recommends considering EU-style legislation or risk-based sectoral regulation, and adding data literacy education.
